challenge.method: Read sections 2 and 3 together and tested both an ordinary-license classification and a separate fallback identity against the publisher’s namespace. Checked who controls SPDX membership and index classification. Read the generated-data warning in its directory context, compared the live and pinned responses, and checked what the legal code requires to associate CC0 with a work.
challenge.results: The fallback’s trigger and extent depend on the waiver in the same instrument. Neither reclassification of the whole edition as an ordinary license nor a second catalog identity follows. An SPDX license-list entry establishes a fact about that list and supplies no controlling legal category. The repository’s “NOT YET ACTIVE” note concerns serving generated docs. The live publisher response independently establishes availability at retrieval. Applying CC0 to a particular work requires an Affirmer’s association of CC0 with that work, which serving the generic legal code does not establish.

limitations: The identity is confined to the English plaintext with SHA-256 a2010f343487d3f7618affe54f789f5487602331c0a8d03f49e9a7c547cf0499. A particular work’s dedication, ownership of rights, and legal effect in any jurisdiction require separate evidence.

The index scope supplies the kind criterion. The exact `active` value comes from the proposal and is assessed only for the publicly presented edition. Canonical admission and release approval remain separate.

reasoning: At the 2026-11-25 cutoff, Creative Commons identifies the English edition as “CC0 1.0 Universal” and places it in its publicdomain category. Section 2 waives the Affirmer’s rights to the extent permitted by law. Section 3 preserves the effective portion of the waiver and grants a license to each affected person only to the extent the waiver is judged invalid or ineffective. The License Index expressly includes dedications under its related legal instrument criterion. The supported prospective mapping is name `CC0 1.0 Universal`, kind `related-instrument`, state `active`. The state describes the proposed index record for the edition verified at the publisher’s live endpoint.
